entries.value: Louis Michel Chablis 2022 is Chardonnay from village Chablis, at the northern tip of Burgundy, where a cool climate and chalky clay give a lean, mineral wine. The domaine makes it in steel tanks with no oak at all, so it tastes of the place, not the barrel: green apple, lemon, white flowers and a chalky, oyster-shell finish, crisp and precise. It is the value bottle for the Redfish Véronique, its acidity meeting the preserved lemon and pickled grapes. We pour it at 48 to 52°F in a white-wine glass, iced between pours. The domaine dates to 1850, and by 1980 it had traded its old barrels for steel.

entries.value: Jean-Philippe Fichet Bourgogne Blanc 2023 is Chardonnay under Burgundy’s regional name, from three parcels in the village of Meursault whose vines average over 50 years. It is fermented in steel and then rests about twelve months in cement, never in barrel, so the fruit stays clear: white peach, lemon and a little hazelnut, creamy, with fresh acidity. It is the value bottle for the Louisiana BBQ Lobster on the dinner tasting, its texture meeting the butter and its freshness clearing the ’nduja. We pour it at 50 to 54°F in a white Burgundy bowl, briefly iced. The domaine was rebuilt parcel by parcel over two decades.
